text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Stock exchange turnover hits record levels, index at highest point since 1995.
- King Hussein orders improvement in welfare of women prisoners.
AL-DUSTOUR
- Finance Ministry says delayed compensation for bread purchases will be distributed in mid-June.
- Al-Dustour learns that visit of Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal delayed until Tuesday. Jordan's Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah says talks will be comprehensive.
- Cabinet decides that families benefiting from government assistance fund can also get help from civil consumer association.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Jordanian forces start joint exercises with U.S. navy.
- Central Bank confirms that depositors at failed Amman Bank for Investment will retain their rights.
- Palestinian flights from Al-Arish to Amman, scheduled to start today, have been delayed.
- Tests show that water coming to Jordan from Sea of Galilee in Israel meets international standards.
- Doctors reject pay agreement with government reached last October.
AL-ASWAQ
- Foreign funds restore vigour to Jordan's stock exchange.
- Central Bank expected to announce this month further liberalisation of foreign currency operations.
JORDAN TIMES
- Jordanian-U.S. war games start; 2,500 soldiers tame the desert.
- Saudi Foreign Minister says he postpones his visit to Jordan until June 7 or June 8.
